en.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
en.statement: A global enterprise is restructuring its AWS network architecture across two AWS Regions (us-east-1 and eu-west-1). Each region has a dedicated AWS Transit Gateway connecting hundreds of VPCs and a local on-premises data center via AWS Direct Connect with a Transit VIF. The security team mandates strict network isolation: production VPCs must not communicate with development VPCs within the same region, but production VPCs must be able to communicate with production VPCs in the other region. Additionally, traffic must be routed as efficiently as possible over the AWS global network. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an inter-region Transit Gateway peering attachment. Configure all VPCs to associate with the default Transit Gateway route table. Apply AWS Network Firewall policies at each Transit Gateway attachment to drop traffic between development and production CIDRs, allowing inter-region production traffic.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Using the default route table and relying on Network Firewall adds significant operational overhead and cost for packet inspection just to achieve logical routing isolation.

options.text: Establish a Direct Connect Gateway for each region and attach them to both Transit Gateways. Use BGP to advertise production routes globally. Deploy separate Transit Gateways for development and production to achieve physical network isolation within each region.
options.explanation: The rationale for this alternative being considered inadequate is that it ends up adding an unnecessary extra layer of administrative complexity, failing to natively solve the core architectural challenge and going against the fundamental principles of excellence recommended by AWS.

options.text: Create an inter-region peering attachment between the two Transit Gateways. In each region, create separate Transit Gateway route tables for production and development. Associate the respective VPC attachments with their specific route tables. Add a static route in the production route tables pointing to the peering attachment for the cross-region production CIDRs.
options.explanation: Correct: Transit Gateway Isolated Routing allows creating multiple route tables. Associating Dev and Prod attachments to different route tables ensures isolation. Peering TGWs across regions requires static routes, fulfilling the cross-region Prod-to-Prod requirement efficiently.

options.text: Create an inter-region VPC peering connection for every production VPC. In each Transit Gateway, configure route propagation from development VPCs to a blackhole route table. Enable BGP route propagation over the Transit Gateway peering attachment to share production routes automatically.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Transit Gateway peering attachments do NOT support automatic route propagation (unlike VPC or VPN attachments); they require static routes. Creating individual VPC peering connections defeats the hub-and-spoke purpose of the TGW.

en.generalExplanation: Transit Gateway Isolated Routing is achieved by creating multiple TGW Route Tables and associating specific attachments to them. Additionally, TGW peering attachments across regions do not support dynamic route propagation; static routes must be explicitly configured to direct traffic over the peering connection.

pt.domainName: Domínio 3: Melhoria Contínua para Soluções Existentes
pt.statement: Uma empresa global está reestruturando sua arquitetura de rede AWS em duas regiões (us-east-1 e eu-west-1). Cada região possui um AWS Transit Gateway dedicado conectando centenas de VPCs e um data center local via AWS Direct Connect com um Transit VIF. A equipe de segurança exige isolamento estrito de rede: VPCs de produção não devem se comunicar com VPCs de desenvolvimento na mesma região, mas as VPCs de produção devem poder se comunicar com as VPCs de produção na outra região. Além disso, o tráfego deve ser roteado da forma mais eficiente possível pela rede global da AWS. Qual solução atende a esses requisitos com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional?

options.text: Criar um anexo de peering de Transit Gateway entre regiões. Configurar todas as VPCs para se associarem à tabela de rotas padrão do Transit Gateway. Aplicar políticas do AWS Network Firewall em cada anexo para descartar o tráfego entre CIDRs de desenvolvimento e produção, permitindo o tráfego de produção entre regiões.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Usar a tabela de rotas padrão e depender do Network Firewall adiciona sobrecarga operacional e custos significativos de inspeção de pacotes apenas para alcançar isolamento lógico de roteamento.

options.text: Estabelecer um Direct Connect Gateway para cada região e anexá-los a ambos os Transit Gateways. Usar o BGP para anunciar as rotas de produção globalmente. Implantar Transit Gateways separados para desenvolvimento e produção para alcançar isolamento físico de rede dentro de cada região.
options.explanation: A justificativa para essa alternativa ser considerada inadequada é que ela acaba adicionando uma camada extra de complexidade administrativa desnecessária, não conseguindo resolver o desafio arquitetônico central de maneira nativa e contrariando os princípios fundamentais de excelência recomendados pela AWS.

options.text: Criar um anexo de peering entre os dois Transit Gateways. Em cada região, criar tabelas de rotas separadas no Transit Gateway para produção e desenvolvimento. Associar os respectivos anexos de VPC às suas tabelas de rotas específicas. Adicionar uma rota estática nas tabelas de produção apontando para o anexo de peering para os CIDRs de produção da outra região.
options.explanation: Correto: O roteamento isolado no Transit Gateway é feito criando múltiplas tabelas de rotas. Associar anexos de Dev e Prod a tabelas diferentes garante o isolamento. O peering de TGWs entre regiões requer rotas estáticas (não há propagação), o que satisfaz o requisito de Prod-para-Prod de forma eficiente.

options.text: Criar uma conexão de peering de VPC inter-região para cada VPC de produção. Em cada Transit Gateway, configurar a propagação de rotas das VPCs de desenvolvimento para uma tabela de rotas blackhole. Ativar a propagação de rotas BGP sobre o anexo de peering do Transit Gateway para compartilhar rotas de produção automaticamente.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Anexos de peering de Transit Gateway NÃO suportam propagação automática de rotas; eles exigem rotas estáticas. Criar conexões de peering de VPC individuais anula o propósito hub-and-spoke do TGW.

pt.generalExplanation: O roteamento isolado no Transit Gateway é alcançado criando múltiplas Tabelas de Rotas do TGW e associando anexos específicos a elas. Além disso, os anexos de peering do TGW entre regiões não suportam a propagação dinâmica de rotas; rotas estáticas devem ser configuradas explicitamente para direcionar o tráfego pela conexão de peering.

en.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
en.statement: An enterprise has enabled 'All Features' in AWS Organizations with hundreds of member accounts and a single Management Account. Compliance policies mandate that no user or administrator—including the root user of any member account—can provision resources outside of the `us-east-1` and `eu-central-1` regions. Furthermore, AWS CloudTrail logging must never be disabled. However, the organization's Management Account must retain unrestricted global access to perform consolidated billing data aggregations and cross-region provisioning of centralized security tools. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Organization Root container containing an explicit Deny for actions where `aws:RequestedRegion` is not the approved regions (using `NotAction` to exclude global services) and an explicit Deny for `cloudtrail:StopLogging`.
options.explanation: Correct: SCPs attached to the Root container automatically cascade to all member accounts and affect all principals, including root users. Crucially, the Management Account is inherently immune to SCPs, which elegantly satisfies the requirement for it to retain unrestricted global access without complex exclusions.

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Organization Root container with the explicit Deny statements. Include a condition in the SCP using `StringNotEquals` with `aws:PrincipalAccount` matching the Management Account ID to exclude it from the restrictions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While this sounds plausible, it is technically unnecessary and redundant. The Management Account is fundamentally immune to SCPs by design. Adding explicit principal exclusions for the management account in an SCP is an anti-pattern.

options.text: Deploy an AWS IAM Permission Boundary containing the regional and CloudTrail Deny statements to all IAM users and roles across the organization using AWS CloudFormation StackSets, excluding the Management Account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Permission Boundaries do not restrict the root user of a member account. Furthermore, maintaining Permission Boundaries across hundreds of accounts and ensuring they are attached to every new role introduces massive operational overhead compared to a single SCP.

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) Permission Sets with inline policies that deny provisioning in unapproved regions and block CloudTrail modifications. Assign these Permission Sets to all workforce groups across member accounts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Identity Center Permission Sets only restrict federated human users logging in via SSO. They do not restrict local IAM users, service roles, or the local root user of the member accounts, thus failing the compliance mandate.

en.generalExplanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) enforce guardrails across member accounts. A key characteristic of SCPs is that they do NOT affect the Management Account, even if attached to the Root container. This built-in immunity allows administrators to apply strict global restrictions (like Region lock-downs) to all member accounts seamlessly without accidentally locking themselves out of centralized administrative functions.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa ativou 'Todos os Recursos' no AWS Organizations com centenas de contas-membro e uma única Conta de Gerenciamento. As políticas de conformidade exigem que nenhum usuário ou administrador — incluindo o usuário root de qualquer conta-membro — possa provisionar recursos fora das regiões `us-east-1` e `eu-central-1`. Além disso, o AWS CloudTrail nunca deve ser desativado. No entanto, a Conta de Gerenciamento da organização deve reter acesso global irrestrito para realizar agregações de faturamento e provisionamento de ferramentas de segurança globais. Qual abordagem atende a esses requisitos com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional?

options.text: Anexar uma Service Control Policy (SCP) ao contêiner Raiz (Root) da Organização contendo um Deny explícito para ações onde `aws:RequestedRegion` não são as regiões aprovadas (usando `NotAction` para excluir serviços globais) e um Deny explícito para `cloudtrail:StopLogging`.
options.explanation: Correto: SCPs anexadas à Raiz afetam todas as contas-membro (e seus usuários root). A Conta de Gerenciamento é inerentemente imune a SCPs, o que satisfaz a exigência de acesso global irrestrito para essa conta sem necessidade de exclusões complexas.

options.text: Anexar uma Service Control Policy (SCP) ao contêiner Raiz com as declarações Deny. Incluir uma condição na SCP usando `StringNotEquals` com `aws:PrincipalAccount` correspondendo ao ID da Conta de Gerenciamento para excluí-la das restrições.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Embora pareça lógico, é desnecessário. A Conta de Gerenciamento já é imune a SCPs por design na AWS. Adicionar exclusões de conta principal para a conta de gerenciamento em uma SCP é um anti-padrão.

options.text: Implantar um IAM Permission Boundary com as restrições em todos os usuários e roles IAM em toda a organização usando AWS CloudFormation StackSets, excluindo a Conta de Gerenciamento.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Permission Boundaries não restringem o usuário root da conta-membro e exigem manutenção contínua e complexa em centenas de contas em comparação com uma única SCP.

options.text: Configurar Permission Sets no AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) com políticas inline de negação para regiões não aprovadas. Atribuir esses Permission Sets a todos os grupos de trabalho nas contas-membro.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Restringe apenas usuários federados via SSO, deixando usuários locais, roles de serviço e o usuário root de cada conta-membro totalmente livres para burlar a política.

pt.generalExplanation: As SCPs não afetam a Conta de Gerenciamento (Management Account), garantindo que políticas aplicadas na Raiz (Root) protejam as contas-membro sem bloquear funções administrativas globais centralizadas.

en.statement: A large enterprise manages a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) mandates a strict compliance policy: no principal in any member account (including the root user) should be able to make an Amazon S3 bucket public. Additionally, the security team needs a mechanism to continuously identify and automatically remediate any existing S3 buckets that were made public prior to the policy enforcement. Which combination of AWS Control Tower guardrails will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Enable a Mandatory Preventive Guardrail to block S3 public access using AWS Config rules, and an Elective Detective Guardrail to remediate existing buckets using AWS CloudTrail integrations.
options.explanation: The rationale for this alternative being considered inadequate is that it ends up adding an unnecessary extra layer of administrative complexity, failing to natively solve the core architectural challenge and going against the fundamental principles of excellence recommended by AWS.

options.text: Implement IAM Permission Boundaries on all roles across all accounts to prevent s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock, and use AWS Systems Manager Automation to scan and remediate existing buckets.
options.explanation: The rationale for this alternative being considered inadequate is that it ends up adding an unnecessary extra layer of administrative complexity, failing to natively solve the core architectural challenge and going against the fundamental principles of excellence recommended by AWS.

options.text: Enable a Preventive Guardrail (implemented via SCP) to deny operations that disable S3 Block Public Access, and enable a Detective Guardrail (implemented via AWS Config and Lambda) to detect and remediate non-compliant existing buckets.
options.explanation: Correct: In Control Tower, Preventive guardrails use SCPs to block actions at the API level (preventing new violations), while Detective guardrails use AWS Config rules to identify existing violations and can trigger automated remediations.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Network Firewall policy across all VPCs to inspect S3 traffic and block public access requests, combined with Amazon Macie for continuous discovery of existing public buckets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Network Firewall cannot prevent S3 bucket policy changes via the AWS API. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data, but does not natively remediate public buckets automatically like Config.

en.generalExplanation: AWS Control Tower provides two main types of guardrails: Preventive (using Service Control Policies - SCPs) to stop non-compliant actions from occurring, and Detective (using AWS Config) to report on and remediate existing non-compliant resources.

en.statement: A Solutions Architect is troubleshooting access issues in an AWS environment managed by AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO). An employee in the 'DataEngineers' Active Directory group is attempting to access an Amazon Redshift cluster in the 'DataLake' AWS account but receives an 'Access Denied' error. The architect verifies that the 'DataEngineers' group is assigned to the 'RedshiftAdmin' Permission Set in IAM Identity Center. However, when reviewing the IAM roles automatically provisioned in the 'DataLake' account, the trust policy of the role created by IAM Identity Center only lists the SAML provider, and not the specific employee or AD group. What is the architectural reason for this behavior?

options.text: The Permission Set was deployed but the automated propagation failed due to a missing Service Linked Role in the target account, preventing the trust policy from being updated with the AD group SID.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Identity Center role trust policies do not contain references to specific users or AD groups. The federation process handles user mapping dynamically during the SAML assertion.

options.text: This is expected behavior. IAM Identity Center creates a central IAM role in the target account where the trust policy trusts the IAM Identity Center SAML provider. Access is granted because the identity mapping is handled centrally by Identity Center during the authentication flow, not via role trust policies.
options.explanation: Correct: In IAM Identity Center architectures, the trust policy of the provisioned role (`AWSReservedSSO_*`) simply trusts the SAML provider. Identity Center handles the authorization mapping (who can assume which role) centrally, isolating the role trust from specific user identities.

options.text: The 'RedshiftAdmin' Permission Set is missing a Principal element within its inline policy specifying the ARN of the 'DataEngineers' group.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Permission Sets and inline policies define permissions (what actions can be performed), not the Principal (who is performing them). The Principal is implicitly the assumed role.

options.text: The AWS account where Redshift resides was not properly attached to the AWS Organizations root, causing IAM Identity Center to fallback to a generic SAML trust instead of an organizational trust.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Identity Center always uses a SAML provider trust in the provisioned roles regardless of Organizational Unit placement. It does not map AD groups directly in IAM role trust policies.

en.generalExplanation: A fundamental concept of AWS IAM Identity Center is how it abstracts the AssumeRole complexity. When a Permission Set is assigned, it provisions an IAM role in the target account. The Trust Policy of this role simply trusts the IAM Identity Center SAML IdP. Identity Center itself enforces which users/groups are allowed to assume that role during the SSO login process, keeping the IAM role definitions clean and decoupled from the directory.

en.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
en.statement: A global healthcare company needs to replicate critical patient data from an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1 to eu-west-1 for disaster recovery. The data is encrypted using AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs). The replication must occur automatically across different AWS accounts, and the replica in eu-west-1 must be encrypted with a KMS CMK residing in the eu-west-1 region. Furthermore, malicious deletion of objects in the source bucket must not propagate to the destination bucket. Which solution meets these requirements securely?

options.text: Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Create a new KMS CMK in eu-west-1. Update the IAM role used by S3 replication to have kms:Decrypt on the source key and kms:Encrypt on the destination key. Enable delete marker replication to prevent malicious deletions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Enabling delete marker replication would cause deletions in the source bucket to be replicated to the destination, violating the requirement to prevent malicious deletions from propagating.

options.text: Use S3 CRR. Create a multi-Region KMS key. Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode. Configure S3 replication to use the multi-Region key.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance mode allows users with special permissions to bypass the lock and delete data. Moreover, multi-Region keys are not strictly required if a destination key can be used.

options.text: Use S3 CRR. Create a new KMS CMK in eu-west-1. Update the IAM role for replication with kms:Decrypt on the source key and kms:Encrypt on the destination key. Do NOT enable delete marker replication. Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode on the destination bucket.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 CRR supports cross-account replication with KMS encryption by granting explicit Decrypt/Encrypt permissions on the respective regional CMKs. Not replicating delete markers ensures local deletions don't affect the DR copy. Object Lock in Compliance mode ensures strict immutability.

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to schedule hourly transfers between buckets. Use cross-account roles and specify the destination KMS key in the DataSync task configuration. Enable S3 Versioning on both buckets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DataSync is not the native or most efficient mechanism for continuous S3-to-S3 replication. S3 CRR is real-time and fully managed for this exact use case.

en.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) supports cross-account and cross-region replication of KMS-encrypted objects. It requires specific IAM permissions to decrypt with the source KMS key and encrypt with the destination KMS key. By default, S3 does not replicate delete markers, which protects the destination bucket from accidental or malicious deletions in the source bucket.

The company wants to migrate the storage backend to AWS to reduce costs, while keeping the application servers on-premises for another 2 years due to latency constraints with local equipment. The application data is frequently accessed and requires strict low-latency read/write performance. A complete backup of the data must be stored cost-effectively on AWS. Which solution meets these requirements with minimal application changes?

options.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway as a Tape Gateway. Map the iSCSI targets to the application servers and back up the virtual tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
options.explanation: The rationale for this alternative being considered inadequate is that it ends up adding an unnecessary extra layer of administrative complexity, failing to natively solve the core architectural challenge and going against the fundamental principles of excellence recommended by AWS.

options.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway as a File Gateway. Map the NFS/SMB shares to the application servers and use AWS Backup to take daily snapshots.
options.explanation: The rationale for this alternative being considered inadequate is that it ends up adding an unnecessary extra layer of administrative complexity, failing to natively solve the core architectural challenge and going against the fundamental principles of excellence recommended by AWS.

options.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway as a Cached Volume Gateway. Configure the application to connect via iSCSI. The gateway will keep a local cache of frequently accessed data and store the primary data in Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Cached volumes store primary data in S3 and cache only frequently accessed data locally. If a cache miss occurs, latency increases significantly, which violates the strict low-latency requirement for all accessed data.

options.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway as a Stored Volume Gateway. Configure the application to connect via iSCSI. The gateway will store all primary data locally and asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots to Amazon EBS.
options.explanation: Correct: Stored Volume Gateway keeps the entire dataset on-premises for low-latency local access, while asynchronously backing up data to AWS as EBS snapshots, perfectly meeting the requirements.

en.generalExplanation: AWS Storage Gateway's Stored Volume architecture stores all your primary data locally, providing low-latency access to your entire dataset, and asynchronously backs up this data to AWS as Amazon EBS snapshots.

es.statement: Una empresa requiere una arquitectura optimizada para un sistema de inventario usando Amazon DynamoDB. La lógica exige lecturas fuertemente consistentes. Además, un panel en tiempo real necesita agregar datos con latencia ultrabaja. El ingeniero propuso colocar DAX frente a todas las lecturas. ¿Cuáles DOS declaraciones describen las limitaciones y correcciones? (Elija dos.)

options.text: DAX opera como una caché write-through y puede cumplir con solicitudes fuertemente consistentes directamente. Esta solución garantiza una alineación completa con los principios del marco de AWS Well-Architected.
options.explanation: La justificación de que esta alternativa se considere inadecuada es que termina agregando una capa adicional innecesaria de complejidad administrativa, sin lograr resolver de forma nativa el desafío arquitectónico central y yendo en contra de los principios fundamentales de excelencia recomendados por AWS.

options.text: Las lecturas fuertemente consistentes omiten DAX. La aplicación debe dirigir estas lecturas directamente a DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Esta arquitectura representa el enfoque ideal para el escenario presentado, garantizando el cumplimiento integral de todas las estrictas restricciones mencionadas en el enunciado, además de proporcionar una excelente rentabilidad y una perfecta alineación con los pilares establecidos por el AWS Well-Architected Framework.

options.text: DAX debe implementarse en una subred pública para que AWS Lambda acceda a los endpoints.
options.explanation: La justificación de que esta alternativa se considere inadecuada es que termina agregando una capa adicional innecesaria de complejidad administrativa, sin lograr resolver de forma nativa el desafío arquitectónico central y yendo en contra de los principios fundamentales de excelencia recomendados por AWS.

options.text: El panel en tiempo real debe usar el query cache de DAX, que almacena resultados de Query o Scan.
options.explanation: Esta arquitectura representa el enfoque ideal para el escenario presentado, garantizando el cumplimiento integral de todas las estrictas restricciones mencionadas en el enunciado, además de proporcionar una excelente rentabilidad y una perfecta alineación con los pilares establecidos por el AWS Well-Architected Framework.

options.text: El modo DynamoDB On-Demand debe estar habilitado para escalar nodos DAX horizontalmente. Esta solución garantiza una alineación completa con los principios del marco de AWS Well-Architected.

es.generalExplanation: DAX proporciona latencia de microsegundos, pero no atiende lecturas fuertemente consistentes, por lo que las aplicaciones deben consultar a DynamoDB directamente para esos casos.
